claim: Open-source planner: 6 gateways reach 98% of a Swiss town's smart meters (modelled)
data_label: open data: swisstopo swissALTI3D + FSO building register, Murten FR, 2026-11
limit: No field data: entry loss, meters per building and the model choice (3 to 16 gateways) are assumptions.
alt: Dark map of the town of Murten with 2,079 building points coloured by LoRaWAN spreading factor and six gateway stars, next to a curve of percent of meters covered versus number of gateways that passes 95 percent at six gateways.
post:
Swiss utilities have to move 80% of their metering points to smart meters by the end of 2027, and a lot of those meters sit in cellars. Where do you put the radio gateways?

I built an open-source planner for that. It takes the federal building register and the swisstopo terrain model, computes path loss (Okumura-Hata plus a terrain knife-edge check), applies LoRaWAN and wM-Bus link budgets, and picks gateway sites from candidate rooftops and poles.

On one real town (Murten FR, 2,079 buildings, 4,466 assumed meters), modelled with my base assumptions:
- 6 gateways reach 97.7% of meters; random 6-site sets reach 70% on average.
- 12 gateways are needed before 95% of meters are heard by at least two.
- With the same assumptions wM-Bus T1 needs 40 collectors for 80%, LoRaWAN 3.

What is not verified: there are no field measurements. Changing only the propagation model moves the answer from 3 to 16 gateways, and cellar loss from 20 to 40 dB moves it from 3 to 11. Entry loss and meters per building are my assumptions.

I could not find an open-source Swiss tool for this. If you plan smart-meter networks: which cellar loss do you actually see, 20, 30 or 40 dB?

Code: https://github.com/VB-Builds/meter-comm-coverage-planner
